summary.conclusion: 34 scanner/Tier-3 signals collapse to 11 canonical entries; the 7 faithfulness findings are preserved as their own channel with cross-references (not collapsed). Exactly TWO genuinely new scanner findings, both Low: (1) DEDUP-15-001 — the totalWithdrawal announced-vs-executed live-balance drift, materially widened by story-048's 6h/72h retiming (merges CODE-001 + PATTERN-001 + ECON-003 + the retiming facets of PATTERN-002/SLITHER-014, Tier-3-reproduced); (2) DEDUP-15-002 — the story-047 global-buffer-redirect cross-client subsidy footgun (merges ECON-002 + PATTERN-MR-003, corroborated by FAITH-15-006). Everything else collapses into existing ledger entries (L-01, M-02 cluster, L-13, L-01-run11, L-02, plus the QA/style cluster), is parked for manual review (2 items, Law-1 visible channel), or is dropped as a Tier-3-refuted / structural false positive. No regression: no previously-fixed finding reappeared.

findings.title: totalWithdrawal Phase-2 executes the LIVE client balance, not the Phase-1 announced snapshot; story-048 retiming (WAITING_PERIOD 24h->6h, EXECUTION_WINDOW 48h->72h, total 78h) shrinks the community reaction window 4x and widens the announced-vs-executed drift horizon, while three documentation sources still claim 24h/48h
findings.severityEstimate: low (operational hazard / anti-rug-commitment transparency weakening; owner-only executor, Law-3 discount applied — NOT a fresh High/Medium)
findings.fileLine: src/AYieldStrategy.sol:822-837 (Phase-1 snapshot announced in WithdrawalInitiated), :846-860 (Phase-2 forwards cached amount), :84-86 (story-048 retimed constants), :414 (stale 24h/48h docstring); src/concreteYieldStrategies/ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:209-240 (_totalWithdraw uses cached amount only for require(>0) at L211, sells shares proportional to LIVE clientBalances at L219-220, zeroes live balance at L234-235)
findings.rootCause: The two-phase anti-rug machine snapshots and publicly announces the client balance in Phase 1, but Phase 2 sizes the actual sweep from the LIVE clientBalances/totalDeposited at execution time — the snapshot is advisory only. Deposits landing between phases are swept with NO fresh waiting period and never appear in the announced figure. Pre-existing mechanism, but story-048 (ad12cb1) made the divergence materially more reachable: reaction window before execution shrank 24h->6h while the window in which live state can drift grew to a 78h total horizon. The docstring (AYieldStrategy.sol:414), IYieldStrategy.sol:101, and registry designDecision #5 all still document 24h/48h.
findings.impact: The advertised 'announced amount, after a wait' rugpull-protection commitment does not bind the executed amount, and the silent 4x window reduction means monitoring/alerting sized to the documented 24h cadence reacts too slowly. Harm dimension: end-users of an authorized client contract (e.g. stable-staker/SYA) whose mid-window deposits are migrated to owner() without the protective wait. Accounting stays internally correct (live balance zeroed, totalDeposited decremented consistently) — this is a transparency/commitment weakening plus a non-obvious owner footgun, not an over-withdraw or theft path.

findings.title: story-047 pools ALL clients' set-aside buffers into one global setAsideBufferRecipient: in a multi-client deployment every non-recipient client's dip-absorption reserve is silently routed to the single recipient, while stale story-042 NatSpec still promises a per-client reserve
findings.severityEstimate: low (Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun + spec drift; QA doc fix at minimum; implementation is FAITHFUL to story-047)
findings.fileLine: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:353-372 and ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:308-326 (single aggregate transfer to setAsideBufferRecipient); AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 (STALE NatSpec: buffer 'returned to the client... reserve to absorb below-par dips'), :318-341 (stale AUDITOR NOTE), :352-357 (setter); IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132 (stale per-client-reserve NatSpec)
findings.rootCause: Post-047 the per-client set-aside return was replaced by ONE aggregate transfer of all clients' set-asides to a single global recipient. With nonzero setAsideBufferSize configured on more than one client, non-recipient clients' reserves cross-subsidize the recipient's beneficiary; a non-recipient client protocol whose underwater-exit machinery expects its own buffer back (the still-documented story-042 semantics) finds its underwater withdrawals reverting for lack of buffer. The per-client setSetAsideBuffer setter still reads as a per-client reserve, making the consequence non-obvious.
findings.impact: Distributional only — conservation verified (Tier-3 bufferConservation PASS: totalSetAside <= underlyingReceived, dust to skim recipient); no value leaves the protocol and story-047 actually REMOVES the old front-run-the-skim self-benefit incentive. The reportable residue is (a) the multi-client-config footgun and (b) the in-file spec contradiction (stale setAsideBufferSize NatSpec vs correct setAsideBufferRecipient NatSpec three lines below).

findings.title: Global slippageToleranceBps couples withdrawal/skim slippage floors to deposit principal-credit: raising tolerance to clear a stuck withdrawal silently haircuts concurrent depositors' creditedPrincipal (at MAX_BPS: zero credit + zero minOut)
findings.fileLine: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:88-93 (setter bounded only by MAX_BPS), 106-108 (creditedPrincipal = amount*(MAX_BPS-bps)/MAX_BPS), 139/168/225/276 (minOut sites)
findings.rootCause: A single slippageToleranceBps governs both the deposit credit haircut and every swap minOut floor; the two legs cannot be decoupled. An owner raising tolerance for an operational withdrawal would plausibly be surprised that concurrent deposits book haircut principal (shortfall reclassified as skimmable surplus) — surprise => Law-3 in-scope footgun. Value stays inside the protocol; not diff-new (predates story-047/048).
